# AGENTS.md — `.github/`

The workflows and the repository's GitHub settings.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `workflows/ci.yml` | On every push and pull request, every job with Avalonia's build telemetry off, since the solution builds a project that takes Avalonia: `build`, which builds with `-warnaserror` and tests all three families on Linux, Windows and macOS; `pack`, which packs every packable project and checks what was packed against `packages.push` and `packages.local` with `scripts/assert-packages.cs`; `conventions`, which runs `scripts/repo-conventions.cs check`; and `Verification tools`, XamlQuality's, which runs the real-code comparison, `tools/real-code.cs`, and the mutation runner's smoke catalog, `tools/mutate/smoke.json`, and builds the headless probe, `tools/probe/`, and `tools/probe.cs`, on Linux |
| `workflows/release.yml` | Templates' canonical release, one `publish` job. On a `<family>/v*.*.*` tag, or a dispatch with `version` and `family` filled in, `scripts/release-target.cs` resolves the family, version and ids, refusing a bare `v…` tag; then it refuses to run without `NUGET_USER` or from a repository the conventions reject, builds, tests, packs the family's projects at the tag's version, checks the pack with `assert-packages.cs --family`, logs in through `NuGet/login`, pushes the family's ids with `--skip-duplicate`, and creates the GitHub Release with the same files, its notes the family's own commits since its previous tag, written by `release-target.cs notes`, and "Latest" only when no tag of any family is newer. Dispatched with `version` blank, it only logs in and reports the preflight in the run summary |
| `repository.json` | What this repository's GitHub settings vary by: description, topics, required checks, exemptions, and `families`, which says which of `packages.push`'s ids release together. `scripts/repo-conventions.cs` applies and checks it |
| `copilot-instructions.md` | A pointer to the root `AGENTS.md` for tools that look here |

## Rules

| Rule | Why | Guarded by |
|---|---|---|
| **A job's check name is part of the `main` ruleset.** `build (ubuntu-latest)`, `build (windows-latest)`, `build (macos-latest)`, `pack`, `conventions` and `Verification tools` are required checks, listed under `requiredChecks`. The matrix job reports one check per OS, so renaming the job or changing its matrix means updating the list and running `repo-conventions apply` in the same change | A required check that no job reports blocks every pull request, and GitHub never says why | `repository.json`; `repo-conventions check` |
| **`release.yml` keeps its file name**, and the credential preflight stays inside it | The trusted-publishing policy on nuget.org names this file, and the OIDC token is bound to the file name; renamed, every login fails | `docs/publishing.md`, step 2 |
| **`release.yml` is Templates' canonical file**, changed there and copied back, with one addition of this repository's: `AVALONIA_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` | What it publishes is resolved by `release-target.cs`, which Templates tests; a local edit to the publishing path is one nothing tested | Templates' `ReleaseTargetTests` and `PackagingTests` |
| The preflight's list reads `packages.push`; the push and `gh release create` take the ids `release-target.cs` resolved for the tagged family; the workflow spells out none, and nothing globs `*.nupkg` | A glob publishes whatever is in the folder, permanently; a policy is checked by eye against the preflight's list; and a second list of ids in the workflow drifts from the first | each family's `PackagingTests`; `repo-conventions check` |
| The release runs `scripts/assert-packages.cs --family` on what it packed before it pushes | A package of another family, or one declared nowhere, would otherwise reach the push, and one declared and not packed would fail it halfway | `PackagingTests.The_release_workflow_checks_what_was_packed_before_it_pushes` |
| Every publishing step is gated on `RELEASING`, and the push also on `NUGET_USER` | A blank-version dispatch must never publish, and a tag with the variable unset must fail rather than create a release with no package | `release.yml`, the job-level `env` and each step's `if` |
| The release refuses to run from a repository the conventions reject, ungated so the preflight runs it too | A problem the preflight finds costs nothing; the same problem found by a tag leaves a pushed tag and a failed release | `release.yml`, step `Refuse to release a repository the conventions reject` |
| `NUGET_USER` is a repository variable, never a secret | A masked value hides the one fact that diagnoses a failed login | `release.yml` comment; `docs/publishing.md`, step 1 |
| `release.yml` holds `id-token: write` and `contents: write`, nothing broader, and the login stays immediately before the push | That permission replaces a stored API key; the token it yields is short-lived | `release.yml` comments |
